clue.text: Chester said to have been ravaged

parts.note: Deva was the Roman name for the city of Chester
said means stated, as in words spoken

explanation.surface: Someone reports that the city of Chester has been laid waste.
explanation.walkthrough: Chester is a city in north-west England; the Romans called their fortress there Deva. 'to have been' is linking.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something laid waste or wrecked: synonyms.

indicators.note: removed suggests the letters of seabed are shifted away from their places into a new order

explanation.surface: A stretch of seabed has been dredged away, so it lies lower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removed' rearranges SEABED; 'Lower' is a verb, to degrade.
explanation.definitionFit: To lower someone's standing is to cheapen or degrade it: synonyms.

parts.note: half a dozen is six, VI in Roman numerals

indicators.note: developing suggests the letters of true are changing shape into a new order

explanation.surface: Six things are evolving into genuine goodness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half-a-dozen' reads as a quantity of something but is the Roman numeral six; 'developing' signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Moral excellence or goodness of character: synonyms.

clue.text: Two varieties of cheese in north London

parts.note: Swiss is a variety of cheese, with holes
cottage is a soft, lumpy variety of cheese

explanation.surface: Two kinds of cheese are on sale somewhere in north London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two varieties of cheese' gives both pieces. SWISS COTTAGE is a district (and Tube station) in north London; 'in' links.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is the name of a district in that part of the capital: an example.

indicators.note: without tells us the copyright letter is taken out of the word for freight

parts.note: freight means cargo, goods carried
C, as in the copyright symbol

explanation.surface: A vessel carries its freight with no copyright protection.
explanation.walkthrough: The Argo was the ship of Jason and the Argonauts in Greek myth.
explanation.definitionFit: Named vessel of the Argonauts in Greek legend: an example of a ship.

indicators.note: preparing suggests the letters of normal week are being worked up into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: An ordinary working week spent getting a painted finish ready.
explanation.walkthrough: 'preparing' rearranges the ten letters of NORMAL WEEK.
explanation.definitionFit: Decorative work with a glassy fused coating on metal, a coated surface.

indicators.note: outside says the phrase for very much is wrapped around the word for one

parts.note: far means very much, as in far better
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A fair-minded person stands very much outside the crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: Even-handed and impartial treatment: synonyms.

clue.text: One with penny, he and Leo found part of planet's orbit

parts.note: a means one, as in a single thing
taken as written
Leo is the constellation and star sign of the Lion

explanation.surface: Someone with a coin, a man and a person called Leo discover a feature of astronomy.
explanation.walkthrough: Leo reads like a man's name but stands for the lion. 'with', 'and' and 'found' are linking.
explanation.definitionFit: The point in a planet's path where it is farthest from the sun, so a part of its orbit.

parts.note: re means about or concerning
porter is a dark beer

explanation.surface: Someone is writing a piece on beer.
explanation.definitionFit: A journalist whose job is producing news copy, so one writing.

clue.text: Crazy like a dog with rabies?

explanation.surface: A rabid dog seems to have lost its mind.
explanation.walkthrough: A rabid dog would be barking (making a dog's noise) and mad (rabid); 'barking mad' is British slang for completely crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for utterly insane; read literally, a dog that barks and is rabid.

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, hence many
the hop is a climbing, twining plant used in brewing

explanation.surface: A gardener cuts back a lot of a twining climber.
explanation.definitionFit: To chop is to cut with a sharp blow: synonyms.

clue.text: After spring, settled things that are favourable

indicators.note: After places the word for settled behind the word for spring in the answer

parts.note: a well is a spring of water
disposed means settled or arranged, as in disposed of a matter

explanation.surface: After the spring, matters were arranged in a way everyone liked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' tells us the settled piece comes second, after the spring; 'things that are' only links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a kindly, sympathetic attitude: favourable inclination.

explanation.surface: An order to stamp out a sport.
explanation.walkthrough: Squash is a racket game played indoors against a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: To quash or crush an uprising; also the indoor racket sport.

indicators.note: include says the word for hector wraps around the contraction for we will

parts.note: to hector is to bully or taunt, to jeer
we'll is the contraction of we will

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper called Hector promises to put us in.
explanation.walkthrough: Hector looks like a name but is the verb to bully, JEER.
explanation.definitionFit: A trader who sells rings and gems keeps a shop: an example.

explanation.surface: A punch-up at an event with no entrance fee.
explanation.walkthrough: A free-for-all is a brawl anyone can join; read literally, something free for everybody.
explanation.definitionFit: A disorderly brawl open to all comers; literally, at no cost to anyone.

clue.text: Second person is gladly received but don't mention it

parts.note: you is the second person; you're means you are
a welcome guest is one gladly received

explanation.surface: A guest is told they are warmly received, but asked not to bring it up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are polite replies to thanks: equivalent set phrases.

parts.note: ado means fuss or trouble

indicators.note: elaborating suggests the letters of point are being worked into a new form

explanation.surface: Someone goes to great pains to expand on an argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking' is a noun here, as in the taking on of a child or an idea; 'elaborating' signals the anagram of point.
explanation.definitionFit: Adopting a child or an idea is accepting or taking it on as one's own.

clue.text: Lewd development with heather at home

indicators.note: development suggests the letters of lewd are reworked into a new order

parts.note: ling is a name for common heather

explanation.surface: Something rude happens among the heather near the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'development' rearranges LEWD into DWEL; 'with' and 'at' link.
explanation.definitionFit: A house or abode where one lives: synonyms.

clue.text: Where rainwater might go and be wasted

explanation.surface: Rainwater runs off and is lost.
explanation.walkthrough: Literally where runoff flows; idiomatically, money or effort gone to waste.
explanation.definitionFit: Into the gutter outlet; also an idiom for squandered effort or money.

indicators.note: during puts the abbreviation for say within the word for wet weather

parts.note: rain is wet weather
eg (for example) means say

explanation.surface: Someone gets back on their feet, for instance in a rainy spell.
explanation.definitionFit: To get back something lost: synonyms.

parts.note: to prop is to support
a cockney drops the h, so her becomes 'er

explanation.surface: It seems fitting to back a London woman.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys (East Londoners) drop initial h, so 'her' is 'er.
explanation.definitionFit: Correct or fitting, as in the right way: synonyms.

clue.text: Girl, say, obtained about £1 from one with many tongues

indicators.note: say tells us the girl's name is heard, not spelt

parts.note: Polly is a girl's name

indicators.note: about puts the pound sign letter within the word for obtained

parts.note: got means obtained
L stands for a pound (libra)

explanation.surface: A girl got hold of a pound from a talented linguist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' links.
explanation.definitionFit: A speaker of several languages; 'tongues' means languages.

clue.text: Be seen in public whilst editing a paper

indicators.note: editing suggests the letters of a paper are being revised into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone goes out in public while working on a newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'whilst' links.
explanation.definitionFit: To come into view or show up publicly: synonyms.

clue.text: Leave taking small weight from island

indicators.note: taking means the word for leave holds the abbreviation inside it

parts.note: to go is to leave
oz, ounce, is a small weight

explanation.surface: Someone departs with a little weight from an island.
explanation.walkthrough: Gozo is the second island of Malta. 'from' links.
explanation.definitionFit: A Maltese isle in the Mediterranean: an example of an island.

clue.text: Some prefix I attached to the plant

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A prefix has been stuck onto a plant name.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads 'the plant' with 'to' joining it; IXIA is a South African flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A South African corn lily of the iris family, so an example of a plant.

parts.note: a shaver's tool is a razor; with the 's it gives razor's
a harp is a musical instrument

explanation.surface: A razor is presented as the shaver's tool of choice, for a crisp outline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shaver's instrument' looks like the definition, a razor; the split is SHAVER'S and INSTRUMENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Extremely keen or well-defined, like an edge: synonymous.

explanation.surface: A pointless, off-limits zone.
explanation.walkthrough: NO-GO means hopeless or futile; with 'area' it makes 'no-go area', a place one may not enter.
explanation.definitionFit: Hopeless or bound to fail; also, as shorthand, a forbidden zone.

clue.text: One giving liquid assets to a bank

definitions.text: One giving liquid assets to a bank

parts.words: One giving liquid assets to a bank
parts.note: liquid assets reads like cash deposited with a lender, but the liquid is literal and the bank stores it for transfusion

explanation.surface: A depositor hands cash to a lender.
explanation.definitionFit: A volunteer whose donations go to a transfusion store.
